prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures an indoor room as the camera wearer turns right from a table and cat on the left (~1–1.5 m away) in frame 1 toward a living room wall and couch (~1.5–2.5 m in front) in frames 2–4, before turning back toward a hallway in frame 5 where a woman stands ~3.5–4 m away facing and looking toward the camera wearer. Brightest foreground values (~0.3–0.5 m, within the wearer's arm's reach) highlight the wearer's hands and held blue cloth at the bottom of frames 1–4, which partially occlude the lower floor and sofa edge, as well as a close object at the bottom-right of frame 4. Mid-grey tones in frames 3 and 4 separate the sofa cushions (~1.5–2 m away and ~0.5–1 m apart from left to right) from the slightly farther wall with framed pictures above and behind them, while dark regions mark recessed doorways and hallways (>3 m). Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly distinguishes the 3D relief of the dark black sofa cushions against the black couch frame and reveals the silhouette of the woman in the dim hallway in frame 5. However, the map is unreliable in frame 5 where the overhead ceiling lights cause a bright white near-depth artifact across the upper ceiling, and it flattens the framed wall art into the wall surface.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete regions across the sequence but leaves most of the room layout, walls, and furniture unlabelled on the black background. In frame 1, it segments the orange cat on the left (~1–1.5 m away, facing right) as a 'dog' in light green overlapping a brown 'person' mask for the dark chair/table beneath it, alongside a pink 'person' mask at the bottom for the camera wearer's hand holding the cloth within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m). Frame 2 contains no masks despite the wearer's hands and cloth spanning the lower foreground, while frame 3 mislabels the dark doorway curtain on the upper left (~2–2.5 m away) as a purple 'umbrella'. In frame 4, a large yellow 'couch' mask covers the sectional sofa (~1.2–2 m in front and to the right of the wearer) with black cutouts where the wearer's unsegmented hand/cloth at the bottom-left and a patterned cushion on the right occlude the sofa surface. In frame 5, a pink 'person' mask outlines the woman standing ~3.5–4 m ahead in the hallway facing the camera wearer (cut off below the hips at the bottom frame edge), while misclassifying a decorative cat figurine on the left wall shelf (~2 m away, above and ~1.5 m left of the woman) as a cyan 'bottle'.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map tracks only the magenta 2D hand keypoints of the camera wearer in frames 1 and 2 and erroneous or distant yellow body keypoints in frames 4 and 5 against an otherwise empty black background. In frame 1, a single magenta hand skeleton at the bottom center shows the wearer's left hand (~0.3–0.4 m away, within arm's reach) gripping the cloth, and in frame 2 two magenta hand skeletons ~0.4 m apart at the lower left and lower right show both hands holding the stretched cloth up in front of the torso. In frame 3, no skeletons are detected even though the wearer's right hand remains partly visible at the bottom edge. In frame 4, the map is unreliable, hallucinating a yellow upper-body and facial keypoint cluster on the yellow-patterned sofa pillow (~1.5 m away on the left side of the couch) while missing the wearer's actual foreground hand right below it. In frame 5, a small cluster of yellow keypoints marks the head and upper torso of the woman standing ~3.5–4 m ahead in the hallway, confirming she faces and looks toward the camera wearer with her hands raised near her neck within her own arm's reach, though her lower body and hand articulations are omitted.
